question: Shared: detection of MCI against cognitively normal older adults from speech (speech/language channel). P-58 uses two memory-clinic samples (English, New York; Hungarian, Szeged); P-167 uses the Framingham community cohort (English). Cohort, features (ASR temporal parameters vs acoustic features), classifier and sample size differ, which condition 1 allows.
metric: ROC-AUC vs ROC-AUC. The record's '67-92%' for P-58 is a range over several metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, specificity) across feature subsets, not an estimate, so the pair is judged on the AUCs the papers print.

figures.P-58: All 15 temporal parameters, nested LOO CV. English (14 MCI/19 HC): AUC 0.932; Hanley-McNeil SE 0.050 -> 0.834-1.000. Hungarian (13 MCI/20 HC): AUC 0.727; SE 0.094 -> 0.543-0.911. Hungarian filler-only subset: AUC 0.912 (0.798-1.000). No intervals printed.
figures.P-167: Random forest on 29 acoustic features, 10-fold CV, 100 MCI/100 CN: AUC 0.87 (95% CI 0.81-0.94) as printed; shorter recordings 0.79-0.82.

matched_figure_check: P-58 reports its result for English speakers, the language subset P-167 studies. English 0.932 (0.834-1.000) vs 0.87 (0.81-0.94): each estimate lies inside the other's interval, so the matched figures agree and the papers' own data dissolve the gap. The only P-58 figure outside P-167's interval is the Hungarian-speaking sample's 0.727, a different language population, and even there P-167's 0.87 lies inside P-58's derived Hungarian interval (0.543-0.911).
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: the highest AUC is 0.932, below 0.97.
reason: The two studies do ask the same question on the same channel and metric, but the language-matched figures agree: P-58's English AUC 0.932 and P-167's 0.87 (0.81-0.94) each fall inside the other's interval. The record's '67-92%' is a mixed-metric range, not an estimate. Only P-58's Hungarian sample (0.727) falls below P-167's interval, and P-58 itself notes that its two samples are different subjects.

quotes.quote: Both the English-speaking (n ¼ 33; New York, NY, USA) and the Hungarian-speaking (n ¼ 33; Szeged, Hungary) participants were diagnosed as MCI or HC.
